Alicia —

Great questions and thanks for the MAP. I pulled a quick snapshot (attached) that maps conservative/expected/aggressive tokens-per-dollar ranges for the eval footprint you described. High-level approach:

- Baseline: model variant = open-llama-like medium (int8) for chat; baseline tokens/$ = ~0.012 tokens per cent (i.e., ~8.3k tokens per dollar) under conservative traffic and small batch sizes.
- Caching: we model two cache tiers: prefix KV cache (session-level) and per-turn soft cache. Hit-rate scenarios: 0%, 30%, 60% -> expect token reduction of ~0%, ~22%, ~44% respectively on our simulated dialogue mix.
- Batching/latency: we provide three operational points: real-time per-request (p50 latency target ~45ms for token generation overhead), micro-batching at 50ms (improves tokens/$ by ~12% with p50 latency +20ms), and larger batching at 200ms (improves tokens/$ by ~35% but p50 latency increases ~120ms).
- Quantization/precision: int8 and q4_0 provide major cost wins; we include quality delta estimates from our eval harness (small prompt sensitivity).

Attached: cost_model_snapshot.csv (conservative/expected/aggressive rows + scenario columns). I'll summarize the key lines for the MAP so the finance team has a 1-page view. Can you confirm the pilot concurrency and avg tokens per session so I can tune the numbers?

Proposed small deliverable for MAP update: concise table with the three knobs and expected tokens/$ effect + one-slide decision rule for when to accept larger batch latencies. If that works I'll loop Karthik for the technical specifics and Grace for procurement timeline.

—Sean

Alicia / Sean —

Quick technical notes to make the MAP numbers actionable and auditable by your infra/finops team:

1) Traffic profile assumptions we used: 40k total sessions/week, avg session length 320 tokens (prompt+response combined), 5% concurrent peak, 95% of calls are chat-turns (small context growth). If your avg tokens/session is higher we need to scale tokens/$ linearly.

2) Caching semantics: prefix KV cache yields near-instant returns for repeated prompt prefixes; we model hit-rate as percent of tokens avoided in generation. Example: 30% hit -> ~22% token reduction because hits often fall on cheap prefix tokens not full response tokens.

3) Batching implementation: our serving runtime supports continuous batching with a latency budget. The 50ms micro-batch uses short accumulation windows and yields ~1.12x throughput; the 200ms batch relies on kernel fusion paths and quantized execution -> ~1.35x throughput in our tests. Note: batching benefits compound with lower precision (int8/q4) but may slightly degrade p95 tail latency.

4) Quantization: moving from fp16 -> int8 typically reduces per-token cost by ~28% in our infra; q4 variants can get you another ~10–12% on some backends. We include fallback rules for quality regressions (automatic canary evals).

5) Example line-items for MAP table (copy/paste friendly):
- Scenario A (conservative): no cache, per-request -> tokens/$ = 8.3k
- Scenario B (expected): 30% cache, 50ms batching, int8 -> tokens/$ = 11.5k
- Scenario C (aggressive): 60% cache, 200ms batching, q4 -> tokens/$ = 13.9k

I can produce a short CSV with those three rows and the precise math. Also note the trade: if you require p50 < 100ms for every turn, we recommend planning for micro-batch (50ms) not the 200ms option.

I'll attach the small CSV in the next message if helpful.

—Karthik
